ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Emily Dickinson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day home sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea

text.paragraph: Vomiting and diarrhea for two days (same-day home visit). [S]

Ms. Dickinson is a 54-year-old woman with stage G3a A2 chronic kidney disease and hypertension who called this morning and was seen at home the same day. Two days ago she developed nausea, then vomiting four or five times a day and watery diarrhea six times a day; a member of her household had a similar illness last week. She has kept down only sips of water and tea since yesterday. She feels lightheaded when she stands. She has taken all her usual medicines, including losartan 100 mg, dapagliflozin 10 mg, and amlodipine 5 mg, each morning, because she did not remember the sick-day advice. She has had no blood in the stool or vomit, no severe abdominal pain, and no recent antibiotics or travel. She has taken no NSAIDs. She has passed little urine today. [S]

value.displayName: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease

list.item:
Viral gastroenteritis with volume depletion (A08.4). Probable viral gastroenteritis, given the household contact and the absence of blood, severe pain, or antibiotics. She is moderately volume depleted, with postural hypotension. Blood drawn at the visit and reported this afternoon shows creatinine 1.66 mg/dL (eGFR 36), up from 1.32 seven weeks ago, BUN 34 mg/dL, potassium 5.3 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 20 mmol/L: a prerenal rise from fluid loss while taking an ARB and an SGLT2 inhibitor. She can drink small amounts, she wants to stay home, and her household can help, so care at home is reasonable with close contact. [S]
Oral rehydration solution in small, frequent sips, aiming for at least 2 L today, then normal fluids.
Pause losartan, dapagliflozin, and amlodipine now; restart them after 24 to 48 hours of normal eating and drinking, after a call to the clinic.
Continue atorvastatin and vitamin D; acetaminophen for discomfort; no NSAIDs or antidiarrheal medicines while she has a fever.
Repeat metabolic panel by the mobile phlebotomy service in two to three days.
Go to the emergency department if she cannot keep fluids down, faints, passes no urine for 12 hours, has blood in the stool, or becomes confused; nurse telephone call tomorrow.
Sick-day rules reviewed again with her and written on a card for her medicine cabinet.

Chronic kidney disease G3a A2 (N18.31). Creatinine 1.66 mg/dL, about 26 percent above her treated baseline, with potassium 5.3 mmol/L, from volume depletion on losartan and dapagliflozin. It is expected to recover with fluids and the pause in these medicines. [S]
Recheck creatinine and potassium in two to three days, as above.

Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). 104/64 mmHg seated, with postural hypotension from fluid loss. [S]
Amlodipine paused with the other blood pressure medicines; restart when she is eating and drinking normally.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, and depression monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Nurse telephone call tomorrow; repeat metabolic panel in two to three days; three-month kidney review at home in early June. Next scheduled visit 1885-06-01: home visit for the three-month kidney and blood pressure review. [S]
